Scheduling lane: film. Current plan: docs/refactor/PLAN.md. Live dependency edges supersede historical sequencing below.

2026-09-19 operative acceptance amendment (docs/refactor/PLAN.md):
Ruling E is already decided: film compiler stays on 1.0 path. Phase plan resolves its ten concrete questions; no research-win prerequisite.

Current disposition, 2026-09-19; governing docs/refactor/PLAN.md.
Ruling E is already decided: film compiler stays on 1.0 path. Phase plan resolves its ten concrete questions; no research-win prerequisite.

Original scope retained below for evidence; fleet procedure/assignments are historical and do not govern single-developer work.

D1A-FILM. Split from D1A (owner ruling C, 2026-09-18). Blocked by D1A-types (bd-01M1CQKRG1A4J4BEWCC78F4TEZ). Needs its own phase plan, written after D1A-types S4c lands, against the public shapes D1A-types fixes (owner ruling D: one bundle per model with composed multi-part films; proposal surface outside the bundle, bound by checksum and receipt).

Carried questions (plan section 4, from three cold reviews):
1. Populate BoundProposalSurface; model law that no node or claim support is anchored on the surface.
2. Render the non-text identity in fingerprint and candidateSet headers; court: same description text on two bundles gives two fingerprints.
3. Film context placement: NarratedWorld only with Held as a typed gap, or Held anchored to the unit interval (ContextStep spans are unvalidated today, placement.scala:84-103, compiler.scala:1674).
4. Anchored within rule (compiler.scala:553-556).
5. Stage 1b provenance for film claims (claimProvenance finds parse calls through spans, :2465-2476).
6. Mention ranking and ids on tick coordinates; MentionPosition(offset: Int) needs an additive position case -- check first, a field change would be a break.
7. Status rule for film claims: SurfaceExplicit is documented as directly stated by the source text; licensing it from an annotator or captioner derivation changes its meaning (StatusWeight 1.0, consistency law 3). Owner decision, including whether generated captions may license it.
8. Anchored evidence/v2 and source-support/v2 rendering; court: one tick moves the fingerprint.
9. The film court: synthetic single-edition film compiles through the same stages, accepted nodes keep their canonical interval union, gaps preserved, no status defaulted, foreign identity refused.
10. Sherlock adapter repair receipts and two-part composition.

Blocks E0 and D1B's end-to-end film proofs; does not block D1B's signature work. Whether it is on the 1.0 path follows owner decision E (open).
